### Trajectory 07 — ferrule geometry, performance benchmarks, regulatory ([Edison](https://platform.edisonscientific.com/tasks/98a30884-4ba4-4b26-b59c-af5779b44479))

**Ferrule envelope — "severely limits stroke" should be softened → *constrains*.** The commonly-cited **19–25 mm is the shaft bore** (shaft OD 7/8″ = 22.2 mm; socket bore ~20–22 mm; socket depth ~36 mm). The **ferrule *outer* envelope is 29–43 mm OD** (US 11,712,394 B1). The bore limits *radial* packaging, but *axial* stroke is set by socket depth. Defensible numbers: **insert volume ≈ 10–15 cm³, available axial stroke ≈ 2–6 mm** in a standard ferrule (up to ~12 mm in an extended 76 mm design).

**Quantitative performance targets (the number the abstract was missing):**
- TPU-only honeycombs/gyroid: **SEA ≈ 0.6–2.9 J/g** (quasi-static); TPU 95A hex ≈ 0.91 J/g @ 47% efficiency.
- **ABS+TPU multi-material: SEA ≈ 4–8 J/g** — multi-material beats TPU-only, and TPU-band thickness tunes peak force.
- PETG lattice: up to ~66.7 J/g (upper-end, architecture-specific — cite as ceiling, not target).
- Dynamic/impact TPU: up to ~38.9 J/g.
- → **Defensible abstract target: SEA ≈ 1–8 J/g and ~30–60 % peak-force reduction vs. a rubber ferrule.**

**Rubber-ferrule baseline (the control to beat):** a solid rubber tip deforms **<1.3 mm under 445 N** and provides *"substantially no shock absorbance"* — transmits >95 % of load, negligible energy per cycle. Crutch-gait peak GRF ≈ **1.25–1.5 BW (~860–1030 N at 70 kg)**, essentially unattenuated.

**Regulatory:** Confirmed **Class I, 510(k)-exempt** under **21 CFR 890.3790** (product code IQO); ISO 11334-1:2007 covers the whole aid incl. ferrule. A novel insert **plausibly stays Class I/exempt** *provided intended use stays "friction surface / tip" and no therapeutic injury-prevention claims are made* — a specific "prevents carpal tunnel/crutch palsy" claim could trigger a 510(k) (predicates: US 11,712,394 B1, WO 2013/073960 A2). So keep the earlier hedge to "**anticipated**" Class I pathway.

### Trajectory 08 — interface fatigue, slip resistance, vibration ([Edison](https://platform.edisonscientific.com/tasks/46e06bf8-385a-4107-81e2-b43a032a2b8f))

**Interface durability — the #1 acceptance risk, and it's a genuine gap:**
- Interfacial **debonding is the dominant failure mode** in *every* studied rigid/soft FFF pairing (PETG/PC-ABS −21–23 % tensile & Charpy delamination; ABS-TPU delaminates preferentially; PLA-PET butt joints retain only ~10 % strength).
- **No PETG–TPU mode-I toughness data exist**; analogous systems bracket it (CFPA-TPU G_Ic ≈ 8–42 kJ/m²; PLA-Nylon ≈ 37–134 J/m²).
- **No high-cycle (10⁵–10⁶) fatigue data exist for *any* co-printed polymer interface** — only 3-cycle data (TPU lattices retain 43–97 % stiffness depending on topology). → Best handled as an **explicitly acknowledged research gap**, not a solved claim.
- Mitigations are well-supported: thermal management (hot-air raised G_Ic 12→33 kJ/m²), reduced layer height (−78 % porosity), interlocking/T-geometry (+58 %), TPU compatibilizing interlayer, and PLA-outer/TPU-neutral-axis material placement.

**Slip resistance — a bare lattice will fail; a co-printed tread is essential.** No crutch-tip-specific COF standard exists (nearest: ASTM F2913/F1677, DIN 51130, ISO 13287; safe threshold **COF ≥ 0.4**). Rubber tips ≈ **0.5–0.7 dry but fall to 0.2–0.3 wet**; a glassy PETG lattice would not meet 0.4. → recommend a **co-printed TPU (85A–95A) tread**, tested per modified ASTM F2913.

**Vibration — do NOT claim it (confirms trajectory 06 + the retitle).** No peer-reviewed study measures vibration/shock transmissibility through any crutch/cane/pole tip. Crutch impact is a **low-frequency (~1–2 Hz) transient**, physically unlike the sustained high-frequency vibration behind HAVS/ISO 5349 — invoking HAVS without frequency-domain data "would not survive peer review or Q&A." → Keep the title on **"impact energy absorption / peak-force attenuation"** (already applied to `crutch-tip-abstract.md`).

### Verdict at a glance

**Both mock reviewers score the abstract 2/5 — major revision** — but for complementary reasons: Reviewer A (Cordero persona) on *mechanics rigor*, Reviewer B (Hofmann persona) on *flight credibility / TRL framing*. Neither recommends rejection; both see a promising early-stage project that under-reports its own data.

### Reviewer A — Cordero persona (architected materials / energy absorption)

**Likes:** timely combination of tensegrity-inspired lattices + BO; building and drop-testing real hardware; multi-angle testing of a genuinely recognized problem (orientation-dependent absorption); BO is well-suited to expensive physical evaluations (literature shows convergence in ~15–250 tests).

**Seven weaknesses**, the biggest being:
- **No quantitative metrics at all** — no specific energy absorption (J/g), plateau stress, densification strain, crush-force efficiency, or peak transmitted force. "Successful payload protection" is unfalsifiable without a success criterion.
- **No baseline** — FDM TPU honeycombs (Bates 2016: up to 0.34 J/cm³) and TPMS/bio-inspired lattices (SEA ~24.6 J/g) are well-characterized comparators; without one, the hexagon unit cell's value proposition can't be assessed.
- **Why hexagonal, and why "tensegrity-like"?** — a monolithic FDM print that mimics tensegrity geometry dissipates energy by material hysteresis, not the elastic self-stress mechanics of true tensegrity (Pajunen 2019 makes this exact distinction).
- **BO loop under-specified** (objective, design variables, noise handling, surrogate) and **strain-rate effects / FDM anisotropy ignored**.

**Toughest Q&A he'd ask:** give me your SEA, peak g, and densification strain vs. a same-density TPU honeycomb; state your BO objective and evaluation count; what's the actual energy-dissipation mechanism, and does the structure survive repeat impacts?

### Reviewer B — Hofmann persona (spacecraft materials / EDL heritage)

**Likes:** build-early-test-often instinct; orientation-independence is a real EDL concern (pitch angle drives peak acceleration); tensegrity landers have legitimate literature heritage.

**Seven weaknesses**, the biggest being:
- **PLA/TPU are not flight materials** — PLA's Tg is ~55–60 °C, both are unqualified for vacuum/outgassing/radiation/thermal cycling (Mars: −120 to +20 °C); aerospace AM polymers mean PEEK/PEI-class materials.
- **Mars framing overreaches TRL** — this is a TRL 1–2 terrestrial methodology demonstrator; his blunt warning: *"The current framing risks embarrassment at a symposium attended by practitioners who have actually put hardware on Mars."*
- **No comparison to EDL heritage** (Pathfinder/MER Vectran airbags at ~18 m/s, Viking/InSight crushable aluminum honeycomb, Sky Crane) and **no mission-relevant J/g-at-peak-g metric**; no roadmap from FDM polymer → metallic AM → qualification.

**Toughest Q&A he'd ask:** ASTM E595 outgassing data for PLA/TPU?; a Ragone-style J/g vs. peak-g comparison to InSight's honeycomb legs or MER airbags?; and why frame it as a Mars lander at all rather than a generalizable BO design methodology?

### Synthesis — top revisions (full 8-item list in the committed review)

1. Report SEA (J/g), peak transmitted acceleration (g), plateau stress, densification strain — even preliminary values.
2. Reframe as a terrestrial analog / methodology demonstrator with a forward-looking flight-translation sentence.
3. Add one matched-density baseline (e.g., FDM TPU hexagonal honeycomb).
4. Specify the BO formulation (objective, variables, constraints, surrogate, evaluation count).
5. Say "tensegrity-inspired," and define success quantitatively (e.g., "peak payload acceleration < X g").

The reviewers *conflict* on framing: A would accept the Mars angle if backed by rigorous mechanics; B objects to it outright given the materials. The synthesis sides with B: lead with methodology, keep Mars as motivation.

### 1 · Yes — there's a strong implant bridge, and it's exactly what this symposium rewards

The framework is **material- and length-scale-agnostic**: the crutch tip is just a fast, cheap, *external*, Class I instance of a closed-loop, multi-objective **Bayesian optimization loop over multi-material architected lattices**. Analyzed Jinkwan's 30-auto-drop drift-calibration run. Data, a reproducible script, figures, and a writeup are committed (`b11bbb3`):

- 📊 **Analysis:** [`docs/drop-test-drift-calibration-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/b11bbb3/docs/drop-test-drift-calibration-analysis.md)

**Setup recap.** Same input-output pair — single-axis **input** wax-mounted on the base plate (CH5, triggered); tri-axis **output** in the vertex key-seat + wax (CH2/CH3/CH4); bungees removed; dummy specimen `prc1kn`. 30 drops released automatically at 13 in, ~15 s apart (from the TP4 `EventTime` stamps). All 30 triggered; CFC-180 is the structural number throughout.

### When did the sensor fall off? **Drop 26 — your guess was exactly right.**

The output resultant is unambiguous: drops 1–24 peak at 5,600–6,500 G raw (255–263 G CFC-180); drops **26–30 collapse to 11–26 G raw (2–6 G CFC-180)** — pure noise, sensor gone. Bonus: **drop 25 caught the sensor letting go** — its resultant spikes to 281 G (z = +9.5 vs the 261 G plateau), with CH3 jumping 2,339→3,453 G and CH4 6,465→7,272 G in a single drop. So: valid attached data = drops 1–24; drop 25 excluded as the pre-fall-off anomaly; the input CH5 stayed valid for all 30.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/b11bbb3/data/drop-tests/drift-calibration/figures/01_full_series.png?raw=true)

### 1) Burn-in drop count: **5** (fresh wax, this rig)

Changepoint scan — OLS the output over drops k+1…24 for each candidate burn-in count k, find where the seating trend disappears:

| burn-in k | slope (%/drop) | p |
|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 | +0.082 | <0.001 |
| 3 | +0.058 | 0.009 |
| 4 | +0.049 | 0.033 |
| **5** | **+0.033** | **0.135 (n.s.)** |
| 6 | +0.011 | 0.560 |

An independent exponential-approach fit agrees: plateau 262.1 G, seating amplitude 8.1 G, **τ = 4.9 drops**. So the transition you asked me to locate is at drop **~5**, not 3–4: the 3-drop burn-in that sufficed in the previous 8-drop run is **marginal** on this longer series (at k = 3 a significant trend remains, p = 0.009). **SOP: ≥ 5 burn-in drops after every fresh wax application** — with the auto-dropper they're nearly free.

### 2) Inherent drift rate: **statistically zero — |drift| ≤ 0.08 %/drop (95 % bound)**

OLS on the stabilized phase only (drops 6–24, n = 19):

| series | mean | CV | slope (%/drop) | 95 % CI (G/drop) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| input CH5 | 215.2 G | 2.57 % | −0.010 % | [−0.52, +0.48] | 0.93 |
| **output** | **261.4 G** | **0.53 %** | **+0.033 %** | **[−0.030, +0.205]** | **0.135** |
| T = OUT/IN | 1.215 | 2.88 % | +0.039 % | [−0.0027, +0.0037] | 0.76 |

No significant drift in any series. The 95 % CI bounds the post-burn-in output drift to **−0.012…+0.078 %/drop ⇒ ≤ ~1.6 % accumulated over a 20-drop campaign**. That's the mount noise floor: in a to-failure run, any monotonic output change bigger than ~2 % is the *specimen*, not the mount.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/b11bbb3/data/drop-tests/drift-calibration/figures/02_stabilized_ols.png?raw=true)

### 3) Regression reliability

- **Start-drop sensitivity:** sweeping the fit start over drops 7–11 keeps the slope between −0.023 and +0.011 %/drop, all n.s. — the zero-drift verdict doesn't hinge on the exact cut. (Starting at drops 4–5 flips it significant — that's the seating tail, which is exactly why burn-in = 5.)
- **Autocorrelation:** Durbin-Watson = 0.61 on the output residuals (a gentle hump near drop ~15). Positive autocorrelation makes OLS *over*-eager to call trends, so the n.s. conclusion survives it a fortiori. Input (1.62) and T (1.44) are fine.
- **Normality:** Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.12 / 0.05 / 0.40 (input / output / T) — no material violation.
- **What limits precision is now the input:** auto-drop input CV is 2.57 % (202–234 G) vs ≤ 0.5 % in the manual runs, and T inherits nearly all of it (output CV is just 0.53 %). Worth checking the auto-dropper's release consistency. Also note T ≈ 1.22 here vs ≈ 1.00 in the prior wax runs — fresh wax + re-seat + auto-rig = a different configuration, so compare T only within a setup, never across re-mounts.

### Bonus: the data saw the fall-off coming ~18 drops early

From drop ~8 the impact steadily migrates between axes at near-constant resultant — CH2 decays 2,272→~510 G (−8.6 %/drop, p ≈ 1e−9) while CH4 grows (+0.7 %/drop, p ≈ 1e−10). The sensor was **slowly rotating in the seat** (wax held magnitude coupling but not orientation), accelerating through drops 22–25 into the fall-off. Two takeaways: the rotation-invariant **resultant (and T) stayed valid to drop 24** — good robustness news — and a live **per-axis-ratio (e.g. CH2/CH4) health check** would have flagged the loosening around drop ~12, in time to re-seat instead of losing drops 26–30. For 20+-drop auto campaigns, pair the key-seat with a positive retainer (clip / set-screw / the tighter #35 pocket) and keep wax as couplant only.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/b11bbb3/data/drop-tests/drift-calibration/figures/03_axis_migration.png?raw=true)

<sub>Caveats: n = 1 specimen (failed print `prc1kn`) — this calibrates the mount/DAQ/rig, not geometry. 200 ms window; Δv partial-pulse (~2.4–2.9 m/s); tri-axis orientation unverified (and demonstrably changing, per the migration); raw input peaks still run 85–90 % of the CH5 full scale. The movie-mode video that shut off wasn't uploaded, so no video cross-check this run.</sub>

### Damage check — `prc1kn` and the sensor, across everything dropped so far

Short answer: **no detectable damage — to the specimen or to the accelerometer.** I read "the two drops" both ways it could mean — the tri-axis sensor's **two fall-offs** (end of the bare key-mounted run, and drift-cal drop 26), and the specimen's accumulated campaigns — and checked both quantitatively across all four `prc1kn` sessions (~48 recorded drops). Script, figures, doc committed (`ceac957`):

- 📊 **Analysis:** [`docs/drop-test-prc1kn-health-check.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/ceac957/docs/drop-test-prc1kn-health-check.md)
- 🐍 Script: [`scripts/analysis/drop_test_prc1kn_health_check.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/ceac957/scripts/analysis/drop_test_prc1kn_health_check.py) · figures + metrics JSON: [`data/drop-tests/prc1kn-health/figures/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/tree/ceac957/data/drop-tests/prc1kn-health/figures)

**Method.** Output *level* and T are mount-confounded across the re-waxings, so the specimen-damage indicators are the mount-robust ones: the **ringdown dominant frequency / spectral centroid** (computed on the sum of per-axis PSDs — rotation-invariant, so the sensor slowly rotating in the seat can't fake a shift) and the **output pulse width** (a cracked/softened structure lengthens the pulse and lowers its resonance, f ∝ √k).

| session | n | input (G) | output (G) | T | pulse (ms) | ringdown mode (Hz) | centroid (Hz) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| key-mounted (drops 1–5) | 5 | 219 | 234 | 1.07 | 1.52 | 519–549 | 665 |
| key-mounted-wax (6–10) | 5 | 229 | 228 | 1.00 | 1.52 | 519–549 | 688 |
| burn-in-wax (11–18) | 8 | 227 | 224 | 0.99 | 1.51 | 519–549 | 732 |
| drift-calibration (19–42 valid) | 24 | 217 | 261 | 1.20 | 1.51 | 519–549 | 760 |

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/ceac957/data/drop-tests/prc1kn-health/figures/01_health_indicators.png?raw=true)

**Specimen — clean bill of health:**
1. **Pulse width is flat across all 48 drops** — 1.51 ± 0.02 ms, slope +0.003 %/drop (p = 0.79). No softening.
2. **The structural ringdown mode never moved** — locked at 519–549 Hz (one 30.5 Hz Welch bin) from drop 1 to drop 42. A cut tendon or cracked strut (the `m6cyoq`/`T3_0103` failure modes) sheds stiffness and this frequency falls; it didn't.
3. The **spectral centroid actually creeps *up*** across sessions (665 → 760 Hz) — the *opposite* of damage. It tracks the mount history (bare press-fit → wax → fresh wax → auto-rig), i.e. progressively better high-frequency coupling, not the structure.
4. Photos: no new visible strut/tendon damage — the lumpy tendon sections are the pre-existing TPU print bubbles that made `prc1kn` a "failed print" to begin with.
5. Corollary: **the T ≈ 1.20 level in the drift-cal run vs ≈ 0.99 in the prior wax runs is a re-mount/rig effect, not specimen change** — if the specimen had changed, pulse width and ringdown frequency would have moved with it. Both are unchanged.

**Sensor — survived both fall-offs:**
- After fall-off #1 its noise floor *improved* (CH2/3/4 RMS 0.34/0.24/0.22 → 0.18/0.18/0.15 G) and it read 228 G at a 228 G input — no sensitivity or zero shift. Drift-cal noise (≤ 0.46 G) is still ≈ 0.003 % of full scale, plausibly auto-rig ambient vibration. Perspective: it takes 5,600–6,500 G raw *every measured drop*; a tumble onto the plate is small next to that.
- No post-fall-off-#2 data exist yet — worth a quick tap check on all three axes before the next campaign. Fun detail: the last valid drop (24) has the **highest spectral centroid of the whole series (843 Hz)** — extra HF rattle right before the drop-25 letting-go spike, a second early-warning signal alongside the per-axis migration.

**Implication for BO:** a fixed dummy is stable for at least ~50 drops at 13 in, so `prc1kn` can keep serving as the rig-calibration standard, and specimen wear-out won't silently masquerade as rig drift on these timescales. Caveat: `prc1kn` is n = 1 *and* a failed print — intact, pre-tensioned prints may fatigue differently (tendon creep, junction fatigue), so re-run this health check ([one command](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/ceac957/scripts/analysis/drop_test_prc1kn_health_check.py)) on the first intact specimen that gets a long campaign. Frequency resolution is 30.5 Hz, so mode shifts under ~6 % aren't resolvable.

### Drift-calibration #2 — 50 auto-drops (`prc1kn`): OLS drift + damage check

Analyzed all 50 drops. Data, a reproducible script, figures, and a writeup are committed (`92c9995`):

- 📊 **Analysis:** [`docs/drop-test-drift-calibration2-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/92c9995/docs/drop-test-drift-calibration2-analysis.md)
- 📁 Data + README: [`data/drop-tests/drift-calibration2/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/tree/92c9995/data/drop-tests/drift-calibration2) · script: [`drop_test_drift_calibration2_analysis.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/92c9995/scripts/analysis/drop_test_drift_calibration2_analysis.py) (emits [`drift_calibration2_metrics.json`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/92c9995/data/drop-tests/drift-calibration2/figures/drift_calibration2_metrics.json))

**First things first: the campaign design worked.** All **50/50 drops triggered, and the output sensor never fell off** — the data confirm it (attached-sensor peaks, 3,178–3,537 G raw resultant, on every drop; run #1 collapsed to <30 G after its drop-25 fall-off). The cable tie-off cures that failure mode for free. Cadence ~17 s/drop, whole campaign ~14 min.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/92c9995/data/drop-tests/drift-calibration2/figures/01_full_series.png?raw=true)

### 1) Burn-in / stabilization phase: slower this time — ~12–15 drops, not 5

The changepoint scan never fully flattens by k = 12 (with n = 40–50 the test now resolves tiny slopes), so I used two independent estimators:

- **Exponential-approach fit:** plateau 242.1 G, seating amplitude 6.9 G (≈ 2.9 %), **τ = 12.1 drops** — vs τ = 4.9 in run #1. Same wax, different application, different seating clock.
- **Split-half check:** drops 6–28 drift **+0.096 %/drop (p < 0.001)**; drops 29–50 drift **−0.021 %/drop** — the seating trend has died out (slightly reversed) by the second half.

So for **output-only** metrics the stabilization point on this re-mount is around **drop 12–15**, and a 5-drop burn-in is not enough — τ evidently varies per wax application, so re-run the changepoint scan after each re-mount rather than fixing a count. For **T**, there's no burn-in at all (next point).

### 2) OLS drift rate (drops 6–50, n = 45)

| series | mean | CV | slope (%/drop) | 95 % CI (per drop) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| input CH5 | 223.6 G | 1.74 % | +0.043 | [+0.010, +0.183] G | 0.029 |
| output | 241.0 G | 0.64 % | +0.032 | [+0.050, +0.105] G | <0.001 |
| **T = OUT/IN** | **1.078** | **1.95 %** | **−0.010** | **[−0.0006, +0.0004]** | **0.669** |

**The key finding: input and output drift *together*, and T cancels it.** The input peak (+0.043 %/drop) and input Δv (+0.072 %/drop, p = 0.009) both creep up — the auto-dropper's strike got slightly harder over 50 drops, a *rig-level* drift, not the mount. Because it's common-mode, **transmissibility is drift-free from drop 1** (slope CI ±0.05 %/drop, centered on zero → |ΔT| ≤ ~1 % worst-case over a 20-drop campaign). That makes `T` the drift-immune BO objective; output-at-fixed-input needs the longer burn-in or detrending against the input.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/92c9995/data/drop-tests/drift-calibration2/figures/02_stabilized_ols.png?raw=true)

### 3) Regression reliability

- **Start-drop sensitivity:** sweeping the start over drops 3–13 moves the output slope smoothly +0.038 → +0.012 %/drop — a decaying seating tail, not a changepoint artifact. `T` stays n.s. at every start.
- **Autocorrelation:** Durbin-Watson 0.43 / 0.73 / 0.55 (output / input / T) — the residuals carry the smooth seating curvature, which makes OLS *over*-eager to call trends. That cuts favorably: the flat-`T` verdict survives a fortiori; the output's tiny p-values mean "trend present," with the exponential fit as the better shape description.
- **Normality:** Shapiro-Wilk 0.23 / 0.07 / 0.18 — fine. And n = 45 gives ~2× tighter CIs than run #1's n = 19 — that, not new physics, is why sub-0.05 %/drop slopes now reach significance.

### 4) Damage / limitations on the structure: **no damage found**

Using the mount-robust indicators from the health check (they can't be faked by seat/wax changes):

| indicator | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| ringdown dominant freq (rotation-invariant) | **549 Hz, locked all 50 drops** (p = 0.38) | no stiffness loss |
| output pulse width | 1.49 ms, CV 0.40 %, −0.75 % total over 50 drops† | no softening |
| pre-impact noise RMS | 0.15–0.20 G, unchanged first-5 vs last-5 | sensor healthy |

†Quantized at the 8 µs sample step; the statistically-significant slope is a 1–2-sample shift pointing *stiffer* — the opposite of damage (a cracked strut/cut tendon lengthens the pulse and lowers the mode).

`prc1kn` has now taken **~98 recorded drops** at ~215–260 G CFC-180 with its structural mode still pinned at 549 Hz — wear-out remains undetectable on BO-campaign timescales at 13 in (for this dummy; intact pre-tensioned prints may fatigue differently). Two non-damage observations worth flagging:

1. **The sensor is still slowly rotating in the seat** — CH3 grows 1,023 → 1,285 G (+0.65 %/drop, p ≈ 1e-17) and CH4 2,945 → 3,376 G (p ≈ 1e-22) at near-constant resultant: the same loosening signature that preceded run #1's fall-off. The cable tie removes the consequence, not the cause — your **deeper-housing suggestion is the right fix** (the sensor sitting only halfway in is exactly what this data shows). A transient HF excursion at drops 16–19 (spectral centroid 660–837 Hz, fully back to baseline by drop 20) coincides with the CH2/CH3 migration inflection → a seat micro-event, not structural.
2. **T level is re-mount-dependent** (1.215 in run #1 → 1.078 here at the same nominal setup) — compare T within a mount only, never across re-waxings.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/92c9995/data/drop-tests/drift-calibration2/figures/03_axis_migration.png?raw=true)

### SOP takeaways

1. **Adopt the cable tie-off** — 50/50 vs run #1's 25-drop ceiling, at zero cost.
2. **Prefer `T` (per-drop OUT/IN ratio)** as the objective — no burn-in needed, immune to the rig-level drift both single channels carry. If output-only peak-g is needed: burn in ≥ 12–15 drops per fresh wax application and re-verify with the changepoint scan each re-mount.
3. **Live seat-health check** during long campaigns: watch the per-axis ratio (e.g. CH2/CH4) — it's the early warning for loosening.
4. **Deepen the key-seat pocket** so the walls, not the wax film, register the sensor.

<sub>Caveats: n = 1 specimen and it's a deliberately-failed print — this calibrates the mount/DAQ/rig, not geometry (T ≈ 1.08 is not a geometry result). 200 ms window; Δv partial-pulse (~2.6 m/s); tri-axis orientation unverified (and demonstrably drifting); ringdown frequency resolution 30.5 Hz, so mode shifts < ~6 % aren't resolvable.</sub>

### 30-drop run on `RW5F61` — CH5 fall-off forensics + OLS drift analysis

Analyzed all 32 captures. Data, a reproducible script, figures, and a writeup are committed (`40f2070`):

- 📊 **Analysis:** [`docs/drop-test-30drops-real-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/40f2070/docs/drop-test-30drops-real-analysis.md)
- 📁 Data + README: [`data/drop-tests/30drops-real/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/tree/40f2070/data/drop-tests/30drops-real) · script: [`drop_test_30drops_real_analysis.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/40f2070/scripts/analysis/drop_test_30drops_real_analysis.py) (emits [`30drops_real_metrics.json`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/40f2070/data/drop-tests/30drops-real/figures/30drops_real_metrics.json))

**Setup recap.** First campaign on a near-real specimen: `RW5F61`, key-seat housings at the top **and** a bottom vertex; TOP tri-axis = CH2–4 (key-seat + wax + cable tie), base-plate single-axis = CH5 (wax, the 1000 G trigger), and the new bottom-vertex tri-axis = CH6/7/8 ("BOT", 9–10.5 mV/G, cable tied). 30 auto-drops at 13 in, ~15 s cadence.

### 1) Which datasets indicate the fall-off — `Signal 11` is the detachment; `11, 12, 17, 27, 28` are the spurious triggers

The classification is unambiguous: a real drop puts ~4,700–5,100 G raw on the TOP resultant and ~1,020–1,490 G on BOT. Five captures have essentially **nothing** there (TOP ≤ 105 G — three orders of magnitude below a real hit) while CH5 still shows 1,650–3,960 G: the trigger fired on the CH5 sensor's *own* motion, not a drop.

| capture | TOP raw (G) | CH5 raw (G) | verdict |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| Signal 11 | 1 | 3,909 | **the fall-off event** — fired 6 s off-cadence, zero specimen response |
| Signal 12 | 105 | 3,960 | spurious (sensor bouncing/settling) |
| Signal 17 | 32 | 2,849 | spurious |
| Signal 27 | 8 | 2,297 | spurious |
| Signal 28 | 2 | 1,651 | spurious |

So **27 of the 30 conducted drops were captured** (Signals 1–10, 13–16, 18–26, 29–32); 3 drops were lost because their impacts fell in the DAQ dead time consumed by the spurious triggers (the event-time gaps around 11–12, 17 and 27–28 each swallow one ~15 s cadence slot).

And CH5 is **not trustworthy on any capture from Signal 11 onward**, even the real ones:
- pre-fall-off (Signals 1–10): CFC-180 251 G, CV **2.4 %** — normal;
- post-fall-off: 42–262 G, CV **34.7 %**, with the raw level stepping between ~3.7–5.0 kG (Signals 13–16) and ~8.3–9.1 kG (18–26 — up to **96 % of the 9,442.9 G full scale**, near clipping) as the loose sensor changed resting position;
- the trigger fired early on the sensor's rattle: the impact lands at the nominal ~3.9 ms on healthy captures but at **9.6 / 9.0 / 5.1 / 35.3 ms** on Signals 13, 14, 15, 26 (that last one only just stayed inside the 200 ms window).

Meanwhile the TOP and BOT channels stayed flat throughout — the structural measurement itself was never disturbed. 👍

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/40f2070/data/drop-tests/30drops-real/figures/01_capture_classification.png?raw=true)

### 2) OLS drift analysis (27 real drops; CH5 excluded, BOT as input reference)

**Burn-in:** the changepoint scan is n.s. from **k = 2** (exponential fit: plateau 264.1 G, amplitude 4.2 G, **τ = 1.4 drops**) — much faster seating than drift-cal #2 (τ = 12); this wax application settled almost immediately. Stabilized phase = drops 3–27 (n = 25):

| series | mean | CV | slope (%/drop) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TOP output (CH2–4)** | **264.1 G** | **0.97 %** | +0.049 | 0.065 (n.s.) |
| BOT input (CH6–8 resultant) | 159.2 G | 6.86 % | +0.428 | 0.021 |
| **T\* = TOP/BOT** | **1.665** | **6.10 %** | −0.324 | 0.053 (n.s.) |
| CH5 (detached, for reference) | 210.5 G | 28.9 % | −0.399 | 0.629 |

- **The TOP output is drift-free and tight** (CV 0.97 %, no significant trend; the split-half wobble spans only ~2 % total). The wax + cable-tie key-seat SOP carries over to `RW5F61` unchanged.
- **The bottom-vertex input works but is noisier than the base plate was** (CV 6.9 % vs 0.5–2.6 %). The culprit is a **level step in the last four captures** (150–160 → 174–191 G) carried by the off-axis CH6/CH7 content while the drop-axis CH8 raw peak stays flat (~925–1,025 G) — the bottom sensor's orientation/coupling shifted late in the run (plausibly disturbed around the same events that freed CH5). That step is also what drives BOT's barely-significant +0.43 %/drop slope and the mirror-image T\* slope.
- **T\* ≈ 1.67 is a different quantity from the old T ≈ 1.0–1.2** — the reference now sits on the compliant bottom vertex, not the rigid plate. Compare it only within this instrumentation layout.
- Reliability: DW 0.36–1.0 (positive autocorrelation → OLS over-eager, so the n.s. verdicts survive a fortiori); start-drop sweep keeps TOP ≤ ~0.1 %/drop everywhere.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/40f2070/data/drop-tests/30drops-real/figures/03_stabilized_ols.png?raw=true)

**Specimen check:** no damage signature on `RW5F61` over the 27 impacts — pulse width flat at 1.53 ms (CV 0.64 %, tiny trend pointing *stiffer*), rotation-invariant ringdown mode with no downward trend, noise floors healthy. The rising spectral centroid and the CH3/CH4 growth at constant resultant are the familiar slow in-seat rotation, not the structure.

### 3) Recommendations — keeping the sensors seated

1. **Base-plate single-axis: stop relying on bare wax for auto campaigns.** It shear-fatigues under repeated ~7–9 kG raw hits. In ISO 5347 order of preference: (a) **stud/screw mount** — bolt a small tapped block to the plate (or drill/tap the acrylic) and screw the sensor down; (b) hard adhesive (CA/epoxy on a sacrificial base); (c) if wax stays: fresh thin film each session **plus a cable tie-off for this sensor too** — the two tied sensors have now survived ~80 drops with zero fall-offs; the one untied sensor is the one that fell.
2. **Move the trigger off the base-plate sensor.** A trigger on a detachable sensor is a single point of failure (5 spurious captures + 3 lost drops here). **CH4 is the robust choice** — ~4,500–4,800 G raw on every real drop, 4.5× margin over the 1000 G level, and it lives in the proven key-seat. CH8 is marginal as a trigger (raw ~925–1,025 G straddles 1000 G); if used, lower the level to ~300–500 G.
3. **Live plausibility check during auto campaigns:** flag any capture whose TOP-resultant max is < 500 G or lands > 6 ms into the record — one line of code, and it would have caught all five spurious captures in real time.
4. **Deepen the key-seat pockets** (as you and Sterling already discussed) so the walls, not the wax film, register the sensor — the in-seat rotation is visible on both tri-axis units, and the bottom unit's late-run off-axis step is what currently costs T\* its precision (CV 6 % vs the ~1 % it should reach). Worth re-checking the bottom sensor's seating before the next campaign.

<sub>Caveats: n = 1 specimen and `RW5F61` is still a failed print (top-tendon bubbles) — this qualifies the three-sensor layout and mount SOP, not geometry (T\* ≈ 1.67 is not a geometry result). 200 ms window; Δv partial-pulse; tri-axis orientations unverified (and the bottom one demonstrably shifted); the CH5 verdicts rest on level/timing forensics, not video of the detachment.</sub>

### 100-drop campaign — analysis + problems found

Analyzed all 100 captures. Data, a reproducible script, figures, and a writeup are committed (`6275e88`):

- 📊 **Analysis:** [`docs/drop-test-100drops-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/6275e88/docs/drop-test-100drops-analysis.md)

### The good news first: 100/100 clean — every fix from the 30-drop run worked

All 100 captures are **real drops** — zero spurious triggers, zero lost drops, zero fall-offs, and the impact lands at **4.01 ± 0.01 ms** in every single record. Moving the trigger to CH4, taping CH5, and the cable ties did exactly what they were supposed to (vs the 30-drop run's 5 spurious captures + 3 lost drops). Cadence was steady (median 20 s; 100 drops in ~31 min).

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/6275e88/data/drop-tests/100drops/figures/01_full_series.png?raw=true)

### ⚠ Problem 1 — the low-range bottom tri-axis is under-ranged: CH8 exceeds full scale on 85/100 drops

| channel | full scale | median peak | max | ≥95 % FS | > FS |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CH6 (BOT X) | 1002.0 G | 73.8 % FS | 106.9 % | 31/100 | 22/100 |
| CH7 (BOT Y) | 991.1 G | 85.4 % FS | 101.7 % | 39/100 | 9/100 |
| **CH8 (BOT Z, drop axis)** | **989.1 G** | **104.7 % FS** | **108.5 %** | **87/100** | **85/100** |

The drop-axis channel spends most of the campaign **above its rated range**. It's not hard flat-topping (≤ 4 samples pinned), but linearity above full scale is unspecified, so **all BOT-derived numbers (BOT peak, T\* = TOP/BOT, BOT Δv) from this run are saturation-biased — don't use them quantitatively.** This was foreseeable in hindsight: the 30-drop run already measured 925–1,075 G raw per axis at the bottom vertex, exactly straddling a ~989 G range. Shock practice wants 2–3× headroom → the bottom-vertex station needs a **≥ 3 kG-range** sensor at 13 in (the previous multi-kG tri-axis fits comfortably), or a lower drop height if you specifically want the low-range unit's resolution.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/6275e88/data/drop-tests/100drops/figures/02_bot_saturation.png?raw=true)

### ⚠ Problem 2 — the taped CH5 creeps upward (~+3 % over the campaign)

Stabilized-phase OLS (drops 10–100, n = 91, CFC-180):

| series | mean | CV | slope (%/drop) | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **TOP output (CH2–4)** | **241.7 G** | **1.01 %** | −0.007 | 0.073 (n.s.) |
| CH5 plate (taped) | 252.6 G | 1.89 % | **+0.035** | 1.1e−06 |
| T = TOP/CH5 | 0.957 | 2.12 % | −0.043 | 4.6e−08 |

The tape held mechanically for 100 drops (a win vs bare wax), but CH5 rises steadily while **TOP stays flat** — in drift-cal #2 a genuinely harder strike moved *both* channels and cancelled in T; here it doesn't, which points at the **tape interface progressively stiffening/seating** under the ~7 kG raw hits, not a real input change. So T = TOP/CH5 carries a slow −0.043 %/drop drift (≈ −4 % total). For BO use: detrend it, burn the tape in (the drift is front-loaded), or upgrade CH5 to a stud/cement mount.

### Burn-in flipped sign this run — and that's informative

Changepoint scan → **burn-in = 9 drops**, but the exponential fit has *negative* amplitude (plateau 241.5 G, −13 G, τ = 7.7 drops): the output starts ~250 G and **settles downward**, opposite to the wax-seating rise on `prc1kn`. That looks like early **specimen break-in** (fresh tendon/joint settling) rather than couplant seating. SOP-wise: ≥ 10 unrecorded burn-in drops covers both signs.

### Specimen over 100 drops: no damage signature, one genuine watch item

- Ringdown dominant mode **pinned at ~610 Hz** all campaign (p = 0.39) — no cut-tendon / cracked-strut signature.
- **But the output pulse width creeps +0.024 %/drop (p = 1.2e−18): 1.496 → 1.536 ms, +2.7 % total** — tiny (≈ 5 samples), yet it's the first campaign with a statistically robust accumulating trend in the *softening* direction, which is what early tendon relaxation would look like. Worth an endpoint photo/reference check after long campaigns from now on.
- The slow in-seat sensor rotation continues on **both** tri-axis units (CH6 raw peak 269 → 605 G at near-constant resultant) — deeper key-seat pockets remain the right fix; resultant-based metrics are robust to it.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/6275e88/data/drop-tests/100drops/figures/05_damage_indicators.png?raw=true)

### Recommendations

1. **Swap the bottom-vertex sensor back to a multi-kG range** (or reduce drop height) — this run's BOT/T\* are not quantitatively usable.
2. **Keep the CH4 trigger + tape retention + cable ties** — validated at 100-drop scale.
3. **T = TOP/CH5** is the usable ratio (CV 2.1 %) with the tape-drift caveat above.
4. **Burn in ≥ 10 drops** on fresh specimens/mounts before recording.
5. **Please assign this specimen its unique ID** — the comment doesn't name it, and the ~610 Hz mode (vs `RW5F61`'s 549 Hz) suggests a different or re-tensioned structure; the pulse-width watch item needs a traceable history to mean anything.

<sub>Caveats: n = 1 specimen (ID unassigned); 200 ms window; Δv partial-pulse; tri-axis orientations unverified and slowly rotating in both seats; BOT quantities saturation-biased throughout; the tape-seating reading of the CH5 drift is inferred from the TOP/CH5 contrast, not an independent coupling measurement.</sub>

### CH4-trigger assessment — 50 auto-drops on `RW5F61`: it passes, adopt it as SOP ✅

Analyzed all 50 captures. Data, a reproducible script, figures, and a writeup are committed (`713bbbc`):

- 📊 **Analysis:** [`docs/drop-test-ch4-trigger-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/713bbbc/docs/drop-test-ch4-trigger-analysis.md)
- 📁 Data + README: [`data/drop-tests/ch4-trigger/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/tree/713bbbc/data/drop-tests/ch4-trigger) · script: [`drop_test_ch4_trigger_analysis.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/713bbbc/scripts/analysis/drop_test_ch4_trigger_analysis.py) (emits [`ch4_trigger_metrics.json`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/713bbbc/data/drop-tests/ch4-trigger/figures/ch4_trigger_metrics.json))

### 1. Trigger verdict — clean on every axis I can test

| trigger health metric | value |
|---|---|
| real drops captured | **50/50** — zero spurious triggers, zero lost drops, zero fall-offs |
| CH4 first crossing of 1000 G | **3.896 ± 0.002 ms** — sample 487 in 49/50 records, sample 488 in the other (**±1 sample / 8 µs jitter**) |
| CH4 raw \|peak\| | 3,472 ± 87 G → **3.2–3.7× margin** over the level, no trend toward it |
| CH4 headroom | max 26.8 % of its 13,624 G full scale — no saturation risk |
| pre-crossing quiet | **≤ 4 G before 3.5 ms in every record** — nothing but the impact rising edge ever approaches the level |
| cadence | median 14 s, 50 drops in ~11 min — fastest campaign yet (100-drop ran ~20 s) |

The rattle-trigger failure mode that produced 5 spurious captures in the 30-drop run has no analogue now: the trigger lives on a sensor that is key-seated, waxed **and** cable-tied. The constant ~0.10 ms offset from the nominal 4.000 ms pre-trigger point is a fixed DAQ latency, identical in every record — harmless. **Recommendation: lock in `trigger = CH4, 1000 G` as the SOP trigger; CH5 stays as a measurement channel only.**

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/713bbbc/data/drop-tests/ch4-trigger/figures/01_trigger_health.png?raw=true)

### 2. The measurement is unperturbed by the trigger change

Stabilized-phase (drops 11–50) vs the 100-drop CH5-trigger run: **T = TOP/CH5 reproduces to 0.3 %** — 0.957 (CV 2.12 %) → **0.960 (CV 1.20 %)** — the tightest T of any `RW5F61` campaign. Absolute levels shifted ~6 % down (TOP 241.7 → 226.7 G, CH5 252.6 → 236.3 G), the familiar re-setup level shift.

**Drift:** TOP (−0.078 %/drop) and CH5 (−0.065 %/drop) both decline slowly *together* (−1.7 % / −2.5 % total), with plate Δv falling in step — the auto-dropper's strike got slightly softer over the campaign, a rig-level drift. Because it's common-mode, **T is flat (p = 0.43 stabilized; full-series +0.023 %/drop, p = 0.065 n.s.)** — the mirror image of drift-cal #2 where a *hardening* strike also cancelled in T. Notably, the 100-drop run's CH5 tape-seating creep (which poisoned T at −0.043 %/drop) is gone this session — consistent with the tape now being burned in.

### 3. Carried-over issues (not trigger-related)

1. **Bottom tri-axis still under-ranged:** CH8 exceeds its 989 G full scale on **40/50 drops** (median 105 % FS) — BOT/T\* remain saturation-biased; the ≥3 kG swap is still pending.
2. **Bottom seat still rotating:** CH6 collapses 849 → 269 G raw at near-constant resultant — same in-seat rotation signature; deeper pockets remain the fix.
3. Minor: TOP pre-impact noise RMS roughly doubled across the run (0.2 → 0.55 G, still ~0.004 % FS) — worth a glance at the top seat/cable before the next campaign.

### 4. Specimen at ~180 cumulative drops — no damage signature

Pulse width flat at 1.51 ms (CV 0.83 %) — the 100-drop run's +2.7 % widening watch item **did not continue** (it reads as per-campaign mount seating, not tendon relaxation). The ringdown alternates between two mode clusters (~520–700 Hz and ~1,340–1,740 Hz, ≈25 drops each) with no trend — two comparable structural modes trading dominance, not a stiffness change.

**With trigger, mounts, retention, burn-in, and drift floor all now characterized, the instrumentation-qualification arc is done — the next campaign can be geometry discrimination (n ≥ 5 distinct intact prints, T = TOP/CH5 objective).**

<sub>Caveats: n = 1 specimen and `RW5F61` is a failed print — this qualifies the trigger/DAQ, not geometry (T ≈ 0.96 is not a geometry result). 200 ms window; Δv partial-pulse; tri-axis orientations unverified; BOT saturation-biased throughout; the "rig softening" reading of the common-mode decline is inferred from Δv + the T cancellation.</sub>

### Bottom-accelerometer options with the remaining inventory

- [x] Gather context (saturation numbers from the 100-drop and CH4-trigger campaigns)
- [x] Work out what the two remaining sensors can and cannot cover
- [x] Compute drop-height / headroom options
- [x] Post recommendations

**Short answer:** with the sensors you have left, no re-shuffle fixes the bottom-vertex saturation at 13 in — the spare single-axis is an even *lower*-range unit than the tri-axis that's already saturating. That leaves two workable paths: **(A) lower the drop height to ~5 in** whenever you want quantitative bottom-vertex data (my recommendation), or **(B) stay at 13 in and treat the bottom channels as qualitative only**, since the validated BO objective `T = TOP/CH5` never uses them. Details and numbers below.

### 1. What the remaining inventory can and cannot do

Full scale on the TP4 is 10 V ÷ sensitivity, so:

| sensor | sensitivity | full scale | vs what each station sees at 13 in |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| remaining tri-axis (the current CH6–8 unit) | 9.98–10.11 mV/G | **~989–1,002 G** | bottom vertex hits **~1,073 G raw** worst-axis → 104–108 % FS (85/100 and 40/50 drops over FS in the last two campaigns) |
| remaining single-axis | 11.61 mV/G | **~861 G** | lower than everything: bottom vertex (~1,073 G) ✗, base plate (6.3–8.1 kG) ✗✗ |

Two tempting shuffles that **don't work**:
- **Swap the top and bottom tri-axes:** the top vertex sees ~3.65 kG raw on its dominant axis ([CH4-trigger campaign](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/713bbbc/docs/drop-test-ch4-trigger-analysis.md)) — that's ~370 % of the low-range unit's full scale. It would also displace the newly validated CH4 trigger.
- **Use the 11.61 mV/G spare at the bottom (or as a CH5 backup):** at 861 G full scale it saturates worse than the current unit at the bottom, and the plate's 6–8 kG raw peaks rule it out as a CH5 stand-in entirely. It's a low-g sensor, full stop.

### 2. Option A (recommended): drop from 13 in to ~5 in for BOT-instrumented campaigns

Peak G scales roughly with impact velocity, i.e. √h. Scaling the measured worst-case peaks from the [CH4-trigger run](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/713bbbc/data/drop-tests/ch4-trigger/figures/ch4_trigger_metrics.json):

| height | worst BOT axis (max, % FS) | CH4 trigger margin (min raw ÷ 1000 G) | CH5 median raw | TOP CFC-180 |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 13 in (now) | **108 %** ✗ | 3.2× | 6.3 kG | ~227 G |
| 8 in | 85 % (marginal) | 2.5× | 4.9 kG | ~178 G |
| **6 in** | **74 %** | 2.2× | 4.3 kG | ~154 G |
| **5 in** | **67 %** ✓ | 2.0× | 3.9 kG | ~141 G |
| 4 in | 60 % ✓ | 1.8× | 3.5 kG | ~126 G |

At **5 in** every channel is healthy: the bottom tri-axis sits at ~65 % FS median with real headroom, the CH4 trigger still clears 1000 G by ~2× on every drop, and the TOP/CH5 signals keep ample SNR. Practical notes:

1. **Verify the scaling empirically, don't trust √h** — the pulse isn't perfectly linear-elastic. A mini sweep (5 auto-drops each at 8 / 6 / 5 / 4 in, ~10 min total with the auto-dropper) and picking the tallest height where the worst axis stays ≤ 70 % FS is the clean way.
2. **Re-run the short qualification at the new height** (≥10 burn-in drops + the OLS drift check) — the drift/burn-in constants were all characterized at 13 in.
3. If the CH4 margin at 5 in feels thin, lowering the trigger level to ~500 G is free — the pre-crossing records have shown ≤ 4 G of activity before the rising edge, so there's nothing for a lower level to false-trigger on.
4. **Pick one height and keep it fixed for the whole geometry campaign** — severity changes the response regime, so 13-in and 5-in results shouldn't be mixed in one BO dataset.

### 3. Option B: stay at 13 in, demote BOT to qualitative

The validated objective `T = TOP/CH5` (0.96, CV 1.2 % in the last campaign) doesn't use the bottom tri-axis at all. You can keep it mounted purely for timing/orientation/seat-health information (flagged as saturation-biased, never quoted quantitatively), or remove it — with the caveat that removing its seismic mass from a measured node changes the configuration, so levels would need one short re-qualification either way.

### 4. Two checks worth doing regardless

- **Pull the datasheet's true linear range for the low-range tri-axis.** The TP4's "full scale" (10 V ÷ sens) is the DAQ ceiling; IEPE sensors typically spec a ±5 V linear output swing, which for a ~10 mV/G unit would mean **~±500 G of guaranteed linearity** — i.e. even the "under-FS" drops may already be outside the linear band, and the 70 %-of-FS target above should then be re-anchored to the datasheet number. Also confirm the shock-survival limit (usually multi-kG, and the flat noise floors across campaigns suggest the sensor is fine).
- **A commercial mechanical shock filter** (butyl-isolated mounting adapter, e.g. PCB/Dytran accessories) between seat and sensor is the textbook fix for resonance-driven over-range while preserving the < 1 kHz structural band — worth a line in the procurement note, but I'd avoid a DIY elastomer pad: it changes the in-band calibration unpredictably and would need a back-to-back check against the high-range unit to trust.

### 5. Where the 11.61 mV/G spare *is* useful

At ≤ 5 in the bottom vertex's worst raw peak (~665 G) fits inside its 861 G full scale, so it could serve as a **redundant z-axis check at the bottom vertex during reduced-height campaigns** (nice cross-check on the tri-axis resultant, though single-axis is exposed to the in-seat rotation we keep seeing), or for low-g work generally — tap tests, the future shaker transfer-function modality, ringdown-focused captures.

### 6. Long-term

If you need **both** 13 in severity **and** quantitative bottom-vertex data, the real fix stays what it was in the [100-drop analysis](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/8f0ad3b/docs/drop-test-100drops-analysis.md): a **3–5 kG-range tri-axis** for the bottom station (the multi-kG unit used in the [30-drop run](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/40f2070/docs/drop-test-30drops-real-analysis.md) read 925–1,025 G raw there with ~10× headroom, so that class of sensor is proven at this station). Until then, Option A gets you clean bottom-vertex data this week with zero new hardware.

- 📁 Data + README: [`data/drop-tests/5in-100drops/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/tree/0325949/data/drop-tests/5in-100drops) · script: [`drop_test_5in_100drops_analysis.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/0325949/scripts/analysis/drop_test_5in_100drops_analysis.py) (emits [`5in_100drops_metrics.json`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/0325949/data/drop-tests/5in-100drops/figures/5in_100drops_metrics.json))
- 📘 SOP: [`docs/drop-test-protocol.md` §6 "Data handling & upload"](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/0325949/docs/drop-test-protocol.md) — batches of **25 CSVs per zip** (~21 MB each, under GitHub's 25 MB attachment cap), Signal numbering kept intact; plus the session-naming and raw-video notes.

### 1. Campaign health — 100/100 clean, fastest run yet

All 100 captures are real drops: zero spurious triggers, zero lost drops, zero fall-offs — the taped housing entrances held both tri-axis sensors for the whole campaign. CH4 crossed the 1000 G level at **3.896 ± 0.002 ms** in every record (±1 sample of jitter, same fixed DAQ latency as at 13 in). Cadence: median **12 s**, 100 drops in ~19 min. The trigger margin thinned to **1.43–1.86×** (CH4 raw 1,433–1,865 G) vs 3.2–3.7× at 13 in — never threatened, but see recommendation 2.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/0325949/data/drop-tests/5in-100drops/figures/01_full_series.png?raw=true)

### 2. The height change did its job — with one big asterisk

**CH8 went from 85/100 drops above full scale (median 105 % FS) at 13 in to 0/100 (max 93.2 % FS) at 5 in.** No channel flat-tops anywhere. That was the goal.

**The asterisk: CH8 looks amplitude-limited just below full scale, not healthy.** Three signatures line up: its raw peak is implausibly constant (885–922 G, **CV 0.4 %**, while every other channel varies 13–25 % drop-to-drop); it barely responded to a 2.6× height change (~1,039 → ~920 G, −11 %, while TOP/CH5 raw dropped ~50 %); and it was deaf to the ~9 % input hardening that both other stations clearly recorded (§3). This matches the earlier datasheet caution — a ~10 mV/G IEPE unit's guaranteed-linear swing is typically ~±500 G — so **BOT amplitudes stay qualitative** until the datasheet linear range is confirmed or a 5-drop cross-check against the multi-kG tri-axis is done. (Also: √h under-predicted some channels and over-predicted others — CH4 raw ratio 0.47 vs 0.62 predicted, CFC-180 ~0.73 — so the "verify empirically per station" step was warranted.)

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/0325949/data/drop-tests/5in-100drops/figures/02_bot_headroom.png?raw=true)

### 3. OLS regression (stabilized phase, drops 11–100, n = 90, CFC-180)

| series | mean | CV | slope (%/drop) | p | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| TOP output (CH2–4) | 164.5 G | 2.52 % | **+0.089** | 2.9e-38 | 0.85 |
| CH5 plate (taped) | 174.2 G | 2.68 % | **+0.094** | 6.3e-37 | 0.84 |
| **T = TOP/CH5** | **0.945** | **0.42 %** | −0.005 | 2.3e-03 | 0.10 |
| BOT input (CH6–8) | 161.7 G | 0.25 % | −0.003 | 6.0e-03 | 0.08 |
| T\* = TOP/BOT | 1.017 | 2.59 % | +0.092 | 2.9e-39 | 0.86 |

**The strike hardened ~+9 % over the campaign — and T cancelled it.** TOP and CH5 rise together at R² ≈ 0.85 with plate Δv rising in lockstep (+0.082 %/drop): a rig-level input drift, not the specimen and not tape seating (which moved CH5 *without* TOP in the 13-in run). The split-half check shows it still accelerating at drop 100 (+0.075 → +0.111 %/drop) — worth a look at the release fixture. **No burn-in transient exists this run**: the changepoint scan never goes n.s. for k = 0–20 because the trend is campaign-long and linear, not seating.

Because the drift is common-mode, **T = TOP/CH5 sits flat at 0.945 with CV 0.42 % — the tightest transmissibility series of the entire program** (1.20 % at 13 in; 2–5 % in the hot-glue era), and it reproduces the 13-in value (0.960) to ~1.6 %. This is the third campaign where a rig-level drift (harder, softer, harder) cancels in T. T\* inherits TOP's rise wholesale because BOT is pinned — don't use T\* from this run. Reliability: DW 1.30–1.89, Shapiro p = 0.20–0.72, start-drop sweep stable.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/0325949/data/drop-tests/5in-100drops/figures/04_stabilized_ols.png?raw=true)

### 4. Specimen at ~280 cumulative drops — no damage signature

Pulse width 1.53 ms (CV 0.53 %, +0.5 % total — the 13-in run's +2.7 % watch item did not recur); ringdown mode still alternating its two familiar clusters with no trend (p = 0.11); noise floors healthy. The bottom seat is **still slowly rotating** (CH7 raw 127 → 199 G at near-constant resultant) even with the taped entrance — tape retains but doesn't register orientation, so the deeper key-seat pockets remain the fix.

### 5. Recommendations

1. **Adopt 5 in as the standard height for BOT-instrumented campaigns** — 100/100 clean, saturation eliminated, T reproduced at less than half the severity.
2. **Lower the CH4 trigger to ~500 G at 5 in** — restores ~3× margin; pre-impact activity is ≤ 35 G, so a 500 G level still has ≥ 14× clearance over the floor.
3. **Keep BOT qualitative** pending the datasheet linear-range check / multi-kG cross-check (§2).
4. **Check the release fixture** for the source of the +9 % input hardening — harmless for T, but it would contaminate any absolute peak-g objective.
5. **T = TOP/CH5 is BO-campaign-ready.** The instrumentation-qualification arc is complete; next up is geometry discrimination (n ≥ 5 distinct intact prints, randomized order).

<sub>Caveats: n = 1 specimen and `RW5F61` is a failed print — this qualifies the reduced-height configuration, not geometry (T ≈ 0.945 is not a geometry result). 200 ms window; Δv partial-pulse; tri-axis orientations unverified (both seats rotating slowly); the "harder strike" reading is inferred from the TOP+CH5+Δv concordance, not an independent release-velocity measurement.</sub>

### Short answer: mostly yes — with two conditions on what "reference" means

- [x] Read the question + context (5-in vs 13-in campaigns, CH8 headroom findings)
- [x] Answer

**If "reference" means what the last few campaigns actually used BOT for — a qualitative sanity channel (did the impact reach the bottom vertex, seat-health/rotation watch, timing) — then yes, the drop height is no longer constrained by the bottom accelerometer.** The validated BO objective is `T = TOP/CH5`, and neither of those channels is anywhere near its range at 13 in (CH5 peaked at ~86 % FS worst-case; CH4/TOP at ~27 %). The 5-in recommendation existed *only* to get quantitative bottom-vertex amplitudes. Give that goal up, and 13 in (or anything over 10 in) is a perfectly valid operating point — and it's already the better-characterized one:

| at 13 in | at 5 in |
|---|---|
| CH4 trigger margin 3.2–3.7× over 1000 G | 1.4–1.9× (I'd recommended dropping the level to ~500 G) |
| T = 0.960, CV 1.20 % (50-drop run) | T = 0.945, CV 0.42 % (100-drop run) |
| ~2.6× more severe strike — likely better geometry discrimination once real specimens differ | gentler on specimens for long cyclic campaigns |

**Condition 1 — "reference" must not mean "denominator."** If anyone later computes `T* = TOP/BOT`, height matters a lot: at 13 in CH8 spent 85/100 drops above full scale, and a channel pinned at its ceiling doesn't just lose absolute accuracy — it *compresses differences* (it was deaf to the ~9 % input drift both other stations saw). So above ~10 in, BOT amplitudes aren't trustworthy even as a **relative** reference between drops or specimens. Timing/presence-of-impact info survives saturation; amplitude comparisons don't. Just keep T\* and any BOT G-values out of quantitative use at that height (same rule the 100-drop analysis already applies).

**Condition 2 — one caveat that cuts the other way:** the 5-in run showed CH8 apparently amplitude-limited at ~920 G *even below* full scale, i.e. BOT amplitudes are suspect at **every** height until the datasheet's true linear range is checked (a ~10 mV/G IEPE unit is often only guaranteed to ~±500 G). So the honest framing is: the height change bought margin against gross over-range, but it did **not** promote BOT to a quantitative channel. If BOT is reference-only anyway, you lose almost nothing going back up.

**Two practical notes if you go >10 in:**
1. **Pick one height and keep it fixed for the entire geometry/BO campaign.** T is height-dependent (0.960 at 13 in vs 0.945 at 5 in on the same specimen) — mixing heights inside one dataset adds a confound that can't be removed afterwards. Changing height between campaigns is fine; changing it within one is not.
2. Sensor survival is not a concern — the low-range unit took 85+ over-FS hits at 13 in with flat noise floors throughout (shock-survival limits are typically multi-kG), so running it saturated as a qualitative channel doesn't damage it.

**Bottom line:** since `T = TOP/CH5` is the objective and BOT is a reference channel, go with whatever height serves the science — 13 in is a well-qualified choice with better trigger margin and higher severity; 5 in gave the tightest T noise floor (0.42 % CV). Just (a) never quote BOT amplitudes or T\* quantitatively at >10 in, and (b) freeze the choice before the n ≥ 5 geometry campaign starts.

### 200-drop campaign on `7xadt6` (10 in, CH5 trigger) — OLS analysis + three problems found

Analyzed all 200 captures. Data, a reproducible script, figures, and a writeup are committed (`a136ab6`):

- 📊 **Analysis:** [`docs/drop-test-200drops-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/a136ab6/docs/drop-test-200drops-analysis.md)
- 📁 Data + README: [`data/drop-tests/200drops/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/tree/a136ab6/data/drop-tests/200drops) · script: [`drop_test_200drops_analysis.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/a136ab6/scripts/analysis/drop_test_200drops_analysis.py) (emits [`200drops_metrics.json`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/a136ab6/data/drop-tests/200drops/figures/200drops_metrics.json))

**This is a milestone run:** first long campaign on a **fresh intact print** (`7xadt6` — every prior ≥30-drop campaign used the failed prints `prc1kn`/`RW5F61`), first at 10 in, and the largest campaign yet. File note: the exports run `Signal3–202` (drop k = Signal k+2 — Signals 1–2 were your failed practice/trigger attempts and weren't exported).

### 1. Campaign health — 200/200 clean, the CH5 trigger was flawless

Zero spurious triggers, zero lost drops, zero fall-offs. CH5 crossed 1000 G at **3.896 ± 0.000 ms** in every record (same fixed DAQ latency as always), with raw peaks 3,609–6,245 G → **3.6–6.2× margin** and ≤ 9 G of pre-impact activity. Cadence 13–14 s; 200 drops in ~46 min, fully automatic.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/a136ab6/data/drop-tests/200drops/figures/01_full_series.png?raw=true)

### 2. ⚠ Problem 1 — the bottom tri-axis dropped out *electrically* for 113 captures

BOT (CH6–8) collapses to the electrical noise floor (~0.01 G RMS — no impact response at all) on **Signals 61–173**, then self-recovers at Signal 174. This is not a mechanical fall-off: on **Signal 60** CH6 **rails at ~1,030 G for ~14 ms** (an amplifier/bias rail), then the whole block goes silent — and a detached sensor dangling on its cable still shows hundreds-of-G rattle (we've seen that twice before); a *silent* channel means lost ICP bias / broken signal path. It recovered mid-campaign with nobody touching the rig → an **intermittent cable/connector**. Please wiggle-test the CH6–8 cable path and both connectors before the next campaign — note the cable tie-off that prevents fall-offs can also side-load the connector (Sterling's point about handling by the housing, not the cord, cuts the same way).

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/a136ab6/data/drop-tests/200drops/figures/02_bot_dropout_headroom.png?raw=true)

### 3. ⚠ Problem 2 — at 10 in the low-range BOT is back over full scale

On the 87 BOT-alive captures **CH8 exceeds its 989 G FS on 50/87 (median 105 % FS) and now CH7 does too (31/87, median 97 %)**. As discussed on the height question: above ~10 in the BOT station is qualitative only — don't use BOT amplitudes or T\* from this run quantitatively.

### 4. OLS regression (stabilized phase = drops 11–200, n = 190, CFC-180)

No burn-in transient this run (the trend is campaign-long and linear, not seating — changepoint scan never goes n.s., exponential fit diverges), so the SOP 10-drop window applies:

| series | mean | CV | slope (%/drop) | p | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| TOP output (CH2–4) | 244.6 G | 1.98 % | **−0.028** | 1.2e-37 | 0.58 |
| CH5 plate (trigger) | 238.7 G | 3.40 % | **−0.036** | 2.9e-18 | 0.33 |
| **T = TOP/CH5** | **1.025** | **2.37 %** | +0.009 | 3.6e-03 | 0.04 |
| BOT (alive drops, n = 77) | 175.8 G | 5.62 % | +0.055 | 1.9e-14 | qualitative |
| T\* = TOP/BOT | 1.403 | 6.54 % | −0.073 | 1.6e-21 | qualitative |

**TOP and CH5 decline together** (−5.6 % / −7 % accumulated) with plate Δv falling in lockstep — the familiar **rig-level drift** (the strike softened over ~46 min; mirror image of the 5-in run's +9 % hardening), back-loaded into the second half (split-half: +0.000 %/drop n.s. → −0.023 %/drop). **T cancels it again** — mean 1.025, CV 2.37 %, residual slope ≈ +1.7 % accumulated (R² = 0.04). That's the **fourth consecutive campaign** where a rig-level drift cancels in T. Reliability: DW 0.37–0.70 (positive autocorrelation → OLS over-eager, so the tiny T slope is if anything overstated); start-drop sweep stable.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/a136ab6/data/drop-tests/200drops/figures/04_stabilized_ols.png?raw=true)

### 5. ⚠ Problem 3 — a CH5 excursion at drops ~140–175

CH5 sags to a 210–230 G shelf across drops ~140–175 (min 210 G at drop 173), then partially recovers; **T spikes to 1.09–1.16 at drops 170–176**, and the campaign's only two impact-timing outliers land at drops 170/177. The window overlaps the BOT recovery (drop 172), so something disturbed the rig there — most plausibly the plate sensor's **tape coupling momentarily degrading** (TOP shows no matching feature, so it's not the specimen). Since CH5 is both the trigger and the T denominator: refresh the tape (or move to the stud/cement mount) before the next campaign. Silver lining — the per-drop T series caught this live; it doubles as the rig-health monitor.

### 6. Specimen `7xadt6` — no damage over 200 drops, one genuine watch item

Pulse width 1.48 ms (CV 0.69 %, −0.8 % total, *stiffer* direction), dominant ringdown mode ~550 Hz with no trend (p = 0.20), noise floors healthy. **But:** the dominant mode flips to a **~122 Hz component for the final 9 drops (192–200) consecutively** (sporadic at 172/179 earlier). Level/width/centroid are unchanged, so it reads as mode-trading between comparable PSD peaks — yet a low-frequency mode winning 9 straight drops at the *end* of the campaign is what tendon-relaxation onset would look like. **Please photograph/inspect `7xadt6`'s tendons and run a short 5-drop re-check** — if ~122 Hz now dominates from drop 1, it's a real specimen change (and our first observed one on an intact print).

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/a136ab6/data/drop-tests/200drops/figures/05_damage_indicators.png?raw=true)

### 7. About the 5-in no-trigger problem you hit

The numbers say √h scaling can't explain it: at 10 in this specimen puts 2.9–5.4 kG on CH4 and 3.6–6.2 kG on CH5, which would naively predict ~2–4 kG at 5 in — far above 1000 G. So either `7xadt6` is **strongly nonlinear in drop energy** (a compliant fresh print can absorb a 5-in impact without the sharp bottoming-out spike — RW5F61, stiffer and much-exercised, only reached 1.4–1.9 kG at 5 in), or the practice-run setup differed. Practical fix either way: **at 5 in, lower the trigger level to ~300–500 G instead of raising the height** — pre-impact activity is ≤ 9 G, so even 100 G would have ≥ 10× clearance over the floor. For this campaign, 10 in + 1000 G worked flawlessly.

<sub>Caveats: n = 1 specimen; 200 ms window; Δv partial-pulse; tri-axis orientations unverified; BOT saturation-biased and absent for 113 captures; T ≈ 1.03 at 10 in is not comparable to RW5F61's 0.96 @ 13 in / 0.945 @ 5 in (different specimen *and* height, so this is not yet a geometry-discrimination result).</sub>

### 30-drop check run — diagnosis of the three 200-drop problems (`7xadt6`, 10 in)

Analyzed all 30 check captures (`Signal203–232`). Data, a reproducible script, figures, and a writeup are committed (`475937b`):

- 📊 **Analysis:** [`docs/drop-test-200drops-check-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/475937b/docs/drop-test-200drops-check-analysis.md)
- 📁 Data + README: [`data/drop-tests/200drops-check/`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/tree/475937b/data/drop-tests/200drops-check) · script: [`drop_test_200drops_check_analysis.py`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/475937b/scripts/analysis/drop_test_200drops_check_analysis.py) (emits [`200drops_check_metrics.json`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/475937b/data/drop-tests/200drops-check/figures/200drops_check_metrics.json))

Run health first: **30/30 real drops**, zero spurious triggers, zero fall-offs, CH5 trigger crossing at 3.896 ± 0.000 ms every time, ~14 s cadence (7 min total).

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/475937b/data/drop-tests/200drops-check/figures/01_three_problems.png?raw=true)

### Problem 1 — BOT electrical dropout: ✅ recovered, but not proven fixed

The bottom tri-axis (CH6–8) is **alive on all 30 captures** — full impact response every drop (raw resultant 1,034–1,622 G), nothing near the dead-block's ~0.01 G electrical silence. But two things keep this at "recovered" rather than "fixed":

1. **The very first check capture (Signal 203) is anomalous on BOT only** — the lowest resultant of the run (1,034 G vs a 1,569 G median for the other 29) and pre-impact noise 5–10× the run's typical (2.6/2.2/1.1 G vs ~0.1–0.3 G). That's the signature of a marginal connection re-seating under vibration — consistent with the intermittent-connector diagnosis. An intermittent fault that stays quiet for 30 drops is not an absent fault.
2. Since nothing was repaired between runs, the cause is still in place. **The wiggle-test of the CH6–8 cable path and both connectors before the next long campaign stands.**

Also notable: the post-recovery BOT level (~1,570 G median) is well above the campaign's alive-phase ~500–1,100 G — a partially-degraded connection during the campaign's "alive" phase can't be excluded, one more reason all campaign BOT amplitudes stay qualitative.

### Problem 2 — BOT over full scale at 10 in: ⚠ confirmed, now on two axes

| channel | full scale | median peak | max | > FS |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CH6 | 1,002.0 G | 70.0 % FS | 90.5 % | 0/30 |
| CH7 | 991.1 G | **102.3 % FS** | 107.6 % | **26/30** |
| CH8 | 989.1 G | **107.1 % FS** | 109.8 % | **29/30** |

Slightly *worse* than the campaign (CH8 50/87, CH7 31/87) — plausibly because the electrical path now delivers the full signal. The downstream damage is visible: BOT CFC-180 scatters 85–200 G (CV 23.8 %) and T\* spans 1.19–2.80 — unusable. Verdict unchanged: **at 10 in, BOT is qualitative only**; quantitative bottom-vertex data needs ~5 in or a ≥ 3 kG sensor. (Everything else has ample headroom: CH4 max 34.7 % FS, CH5 max 49.0 % FS.)

### Problem 3 — CH5 excursion: ✗ the sensitivity loss persisted — re-mount CH5

| quantity | campaign healthy | campaign excursion | **check run** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| CH5 CFC-180 | 242.2 G | 224.7 G | **219.7 G** (CV 1.14 %) |
| TOP CFC-180 | 244.6 G | — | 239.1 G (CV 1.13 %) |
| T = TOP/CH5 | 1.025 | 1.09–1.16 | **1.088** (CV 0.99 %) |

TOP is within ~2 % of its campaign level, but **CH5 sits ~9 % below its healthy level — below even the excursion shelf** — so T is biased up to 1.088, inside the excursion band. The differential (TOP unchanged, CH5 down) rules out a softer strike — every prior rig-level drift moved both channels together — so this is the **tape coupling durably degraded**, not recovered. The degraded state is at least stable (CH5 flat within the run, p = 0.44; T CV 0.99 % is the tightest of any `7xadt6` series), i.e. the coupling settled at a new lower sensitivity rather than continuing to slide.

**Action:** re-mount CH5 (fresh tape at minimum; stud/cement preferred) before the next campaign, then re-baseline T — the "compare T within a mount only" rule applies to the re-mount.

![](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/475937b/data/drop-tests/200drops-check/figures/02_transmissibility_122hz.png?raw=true)

### Bonus — the ~122 Hz watch item: ✅ cleared, no specimen damage

This run doubled as the 5-drop re-check I asked for, and it's good news: the dominant ringdown mode is **back at 519–580 Hz on all 30/30 drops from drop 1**; the ~122 Hz component is present but subdominant throughout (band-power ratio vs ~550 Hz: median 0.26, never ≥ 1). Pulse width 1.482 ms (CV 0.29 %, flat, matching the campaign's 1.48 ms). The final-9-drop low-mode dominance was **transient mode-trading, not tendon-relaxation onset** — `7xadt6` shows no damage signature at ~230 cumulative drops. (Minor: the 122/550 ratio creeps up mildly within the run, 0.13 → 0.43, p = 0.013 — the per-drop ratio is now in the metrics JSON so future campaigns can watch it directly.)

### Bottom line

| item | verdict | action |
|---|---|---|
| 1. BOT dropout | recovered (30/30) but cause untouched; Signal 203 says still marginal | wiggle-test CH6–8 cable + connectors |
| 2. BOT saturation | confirmed, CH7 **and** CH8 over FS at 10 in | keep BOT qualitative, or 5 in / ≥ 3 kG sensor |
| 3. CH5 excursion | **persisted** — coupling down ~9 %, T biased to 1.088 | re-mount CH5, re-baseline T |
| ~122 Hz mode | cleared — transient mode-trading, no damage | none; ratio now tracked in metrics |

<sub>Caveats: n = 1 specimen; 30 drops is short for catching an intermittent electrical fault; 200 ms window; tri-axis orientations unverified; BOT saturation-biased throughout; the CH5 verdict is inferred from the TOP/CH5 differential, not an independent coupling measurement.</sub>

### Why the CH4 and CH5 triggers (1000 G) missed the 5-in drops on `7xadt6`

- [x] Gather context (referenced comment chain → the 5-in no-trigger question from the 200-drop campaign, §7 of [`docs/drop-test-200drops-analysis.md`](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/copilot/add-drop-test-protocol/docs/drop-test-200drops-analysis.md))
- [x] Pull the measured trigger margins from all committed campaigns (13 in, 10 in, 5 in)
- [x] Present the reasons, ranked by evidence
- [x] Post final answer (question only — no code/data changes needed)

First, the measured raw peaks vs. the 1000 G trigger level across the program — the trigger acts on the **raw instantaneous** signal, so these raw numbers (not the CFC-180 ones) are what matters:

| run | CH4 raw \|peak\| | CH5 raw \|peak\| | margin over 1000 G |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `RW5F61`, 13 in (CH4-trigger, 50 drops) | 3,239–3,655 G | 5,500–8,100 G | 3.2–8.1× |
| `7xadt6`, 10 in (200 drops) | 2,951–5,370 G | 3,609–6,245 G | 3.0–6.2× |
| `RW5F61`, **5 in** (100 drops) | **1,433–1,865 G** | 1,964–3,104 G | **1.43×** worst case |
| `7xadt6`, **5 in** (practice) | *no trigger* | *no trigger* | **< 1×** on both |

So at 5 in the margin was already nearly gone in the best-documented case, and on `7xadt6` it evidently crossed below 1. The likely reasons, ranked:

### 1. The 1000 G level left almost no margin at 5 in to begin with
The `RW5F61` 5-in campaign bottomed out at **1,433 G on CH4 — only 1.43× the level** ([5-in analysis §1](https://github.com/vertical-cloud-lab/tensegrity-optimization/blob/copilot/add-drop-test-protocol/docs/drop-test-5in-100drops-analysis.md)). That analysis explicitly recommended lowering the trigger to ~500 G for 5-in work *before* the `7xadt6` practice drops happened. With only ~30 % of headroom, any one of the effects below is enough to kill the trigger; several likely stacked.

### 2. The raw spike collapses much faster than √h
√h scaling from `7xadt6`'s 10-in peaks predicts ~2.1–3.8 kG (CH4) and ~2.6–4.4 kG (CH5) at 5 in — "safely" above 1000 G. But the raw spike is a **short bottoming-out transient that is strongly nonlinear in drop energy**: measured 13 → 5 in on `RW5F61`, CH4's raw peak fell to **0.47×** where √h predicted 0.62× (the CFC-180 level only fell to ~0.73×). The trigger listens to exactly the part of the waveform that dies fastest as severity drops, so √h intuition systematically overestimates trigger margin at low heights.

### 3. `7xadt6` is a fresh, compliant print; `RW5F61` was a stiff, exercised one
The 1.43× margin was measured on a failed print with ~280 cumulative drops — a much stiffer structure. A **compliant intact tensegrity can absorb a 5-in impact without the sharp bottoming-out** that generates the kG-scale spike at the TOP station, keeping CH4 sub-kG entirely. If this is what happened, it's actually useful signal (severity sweeps may discriminate geometry better than a fixed height) — reading 1 in the 200-drop analysis §7.

### 4. CH4 is a single axis of a demonstrably rotating tri-axis
The trigger fires on one axis, not the resultant, and both key seats **rotate in their pockets** (CH7 raw went 127 → 199 G at near-constant resultant; CH4's own raw peak drifted +24 % over the 5-in campaign while the resultant rose only ~9 %). Sensors were re-seated for the new specimen with orientation unverified — an unfavorable seat rotation on setup day takes tens of percent off the axis-projected raw peak, which the thin margin couldn't afford.

### 5. CH5's tape coupling attenuates exactly the frequencies the trigger needs
Tape is a compliant mount that low-passes the kHz content the raw spike is made of, and its state demonstrably moves around: the 200-drop campaign caught a mid-campaign CH5 excursion, and both check runs show the coupling **durably stepped down ~6–8 %** (T stuck at 1.083 vs healthy 1.025) — and that's at CFC-180; the attenuation of the raw high-frequency spike is larger. A soft/fresh tape layer on practice day plausibly shaved CH5's spike substantially.

### 6. A setup/load-path difference can't be excluded — and never can be
For CH5 in particular, the arithmetic is demanding: its weakest 10-in peak was 3,609 G, so missing at 5 in requires a collapse to **< 28 %** — steeper than anything measured from height alone. That points to a contribution from the coupling (reason 5) and/or a genuine rig difference at the 5-in setting. There's precedent for the latter: the clip-height experiment produced **0/8 no-trigger drops with a perfectly healthy sensor chain**, purely from load path, and the release fixture at the 5-in setting was already flagged (the +9 % monotonic input hardening). The catch is structural: **an untriggered drop records nothing**, so no waveform exists to falsify any of this — which is itself the strongest argument for the fix below.

### The fix (already in the SOP)
**Trigger level, not height, is the severity knob.** Pre-impact activity is ≤ 9–35 G in every campaign, so at 5 in a **300–500 G level** restores ~3× margin with ≥ 10× clearance above the noise floor (even 100 G would be safe). If 5-in campaigns are wanted for `7xadt6`-class fresh prints, drop the level first and run one practice capture to measure the actual raw peaks — that single waveform would tell us which of reasons 2–6 dominated.

| metric | 5 in | 10 in | 10/5 ratio |
